subsystems.name: Vacuum can and radiation shields
subsystems.role: insulates the cold stages from room-temperature heat.
parts: copper shields at roughly 50 K and 4 K

subsystems.name: Pre-cooling stage
subsystems.role: gets the machine down to a few kelvin, where the helium mixture can condense.

subsystems.name: Still and heat exchangers
subsystems.role: distils helium-3 out of the mixture and pre-cools it on the way back down.
parts: sintered copper or continuous heat exchangers

subsystems.name: Mixing chamber
subsystems.role: the cold heart: heat is absorbed where concentrated and dilute helium-3 phases meet.
parts: sintered silver or copper heat-exchange surface

subsystems.name: Circulation system
subsystems.role: keeps helium-3 flowing so the cooling cycle is continuous.

subsystems.name: Wiring and signal chain
subsystems.role: carries control and readout signals down to the sample without dumping too much heat or noise.
parts: thermal anchoring at each temperature plate

subsystems.name: Vibration and magnetic isolation
subsystems.role: keeps mechanical noise and stray fields away from sensitive qubits.

buildSteps.title: Design the heat budget
buildSteps.detail: Every support strut, cable and connector is counted: heat conducted down, radiated in, and deposited by changing magnetic fields. The refrigerator is sized so the mixing chamber still has spare cooling power at its base temperature.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the vacuum and shield stack
buildSteps.detail: Stainless-steel vacuum cans and copper shields are machined, welded, polished to reduce emissivity, and assembled with seals that survive repeated cool-downs.

buildSteps.title: Build the pre-cooling stage
buildSteps.detail: A pulse-tube cryocooler (or a liquid-helium bath) is mounted and coupled to the 4 K plate, and a pumped 1 K pot is fitted below it.

buildSteps.title: Assemble still, exchangers and mixing chamber
buildSteps.detail: The still, a stack of heat exchangers and the mixing chamber are joined with leak-tight joints; the mixing chamber is packed with sintered metal to give the phase boundary a large area.

buildSteps.title: Install the gas handling system
buildSteps.detail: Room-temperature pumps, valves, purifier and helium-3 storage are plumbed to the still and the return line, and the precise helium-3/helium-4 mixture is charged into the sealed circuit.

buildSteps.title: Wire and shield the sample stage
buildSteps.detail: Cables are run from room temperature down through attenuators and filters, anchored at each plate so heat is intercepted before it reaches the millikelvin stage; magnetic shielding goes around the sample space.

buildSteps.title: Evacuate, bake and leak-check
buildSteps.detail: The vacuum space is pumped and gently baked to remove water and helium contamination, then tested for leaks — a tiny leak ruins the insulation.

buildSteps.title: Cool down and condense
buildSteps.detail: The cryocooler runs, the mixture condenses and collects in the mixing chamber, the still is pumped, and circulation begins, drawing the temperature down toward the base.

buildSteps.title: Commission and hold
buildSteps.detail: Base temperature, cooling power and stability are measured with the sample wiring attached, then the unit is left running for weeks — long holds are the whole point.

prerequisites.why: it is the working fluid; it is scarce and expensive because it comes mainly from tritium decay and stockpile processing, so recovery and leak-tightness matter.
they provide the 4 K pre-cooling without a liquid-helium supply, which is what makes cryogen-free refrigerators practical in labs.

prerequisites.tech: Cryogenic wiring, filtering and thermal anchoring
prerequisites.why: a single poorly anchored cable can add more heat than the mixing chamber can remove.
superconducting qubits lose coherence to mechanical noise and stray magnetic fields.
they are the main demand driver, and their required qubit counts set how much cooling power and wiring the refrigerator must supply.

pathway.milestone: cryogen-free dilution refrigerators hold samples below about 10 mK for weeks with hundreds of coaxial lines
pathway.unlocks: today's small superconducting-qubit processors and low-temperature physics experiments.

pathway.milestone: bigger mixing chambers and higher cooling power for thousands of qubits
pathway.unlocks: larger processors, but cooling power falls steeply below 100 mK, so heat per qubit must drop too.

pathway.milestone: multiplexing and cryogenic control electronics inside the refrigerator
pathway.unlocks: far fewer cables from room temperature, which is currently the dominant heat and cost problem.

pathway.milestone: modular or higher-temperature qubit architectures that relax the millikelvin requirement
pathway.unlocks: systems where dilution refrigeration is one stage rather than the whole constraint.
